en.title: Substrings Whose Top Frequency Does Not Exceed the Number of Distinct Characters
en.description:
The string contains only a..g. Count the non-empty contiguous substrings in which the highest character frequency does not exceed the number of distinct characters.

The standard I/O, examples, and judging were written independently by CSWork; conventions marked as this site's are not presented as original source constraints.
en.input: A single line containing a string over a..g, of length 1..100000.
en.explanation: Example 1: the four single characters, the two length-2 substrings ab and ba, and the two length-3 substrings aba and baa are valid, 8 in total; aa and abaa are not valid. Example 2: a single character has frequency 1 and 1 distinct character, so it is valid. Example 3: all six non-empty substrings are valid.
hints: A valid substring has at most 7 distinct characters, each appearing at most 7 times, so its length is at most 49. From each left end, extend at most 49 positions while maintaining the frequencies, the number of distinct characters, and the maximum frequency.
